request.goal: Minimize maximum-rank clean step_ms for the source's complete accumulated training step, taking aligned rank maxima before the median over repeats. Retain the original step_ms <= 1.05x original-baseline constraint, all workload, precision, full quality and exact rank-replica requirements and the completion boundary. Communication kernel duration remains a separately profiled diagnostic, not wire time or the primary score.
notes: Command provenance (user command in inputs/intent.json): torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=2 gpt2_ddp_training.py --output /tmp/original-ddp-step --profile, run from the repository root; equivalent to the launch documented in README.md:37 (python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 .../gpt2_ddp_training.py). Source defaults apply to unspecified flags: --warmup 2, --repeats 5, --workloads <repo>/workloads.json (common.py:21-27). The --output directory holds harness artifacts only (rank-{rank}.json, result.json, chrome traces); the evaluator uses its own output location.

Source-required precision and numerical policies: FP32 weights/activations/gradients/optimizer (gpt2_ddp_training.py:27 .float()); TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark=False, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest') (common.py:34-42); dropout fully disabled (resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.0) and use_cache=False (gpt2_ddp_training.py:26); deterministic seeded init (torch.manual_seed(20261020)) and seeded per-rank inputs (torch.Generator seed 31000+source_rank, randint over vocab 50257, gpt2_ddp_training.py:24-33). attn_implementation='eager' is the source's pinned attention numerics used for both the measured model and the in-script reference; a semantics-equivalent alternative is admissible only if the gradient/parameter tolerances against the eager reference still hold.

Measured region (gpt2_ddp_training.py:111-119): before each timed repeat the source restores initial weights, calls torch.cuda.synchronize(), executes a gloo control-group barrier and resets CUDA peak-memory stats, all outside the timer; the timer (time.perf_counter_ns) wraps only step(). Also outside the measured work: model/optimizer/input construction, the one-time rank-0 reference construction and all correctness checks, the 3 profiled diagnostic invocations, the separate bucket-inventory pass, and report writing. Host-to-device input transfer happens once during setup (make_inputs), never inside timing.

State semantics: each warmup/measured/profiled invocation starts from the identical captured initial state (initial state_dict captured right after seeded construction, gpt2_ddp_training.py:62; reset() = raw_model.load_state_dict(initial), :99-100); accumulate() zeroes gradients at entry (set_to_none=True, :37); SGD with momentum=0.0 holds no persistent optimizer state, so every repeated step is semantically idempotent. The evaluator must restore this initial state between invocations without including the restoration in the measurement.

Score aggregation (gpt2_ddp_training.py:149-152 with common.py:66-71): for each aligned repeat index i, step_ms = max over the two ranks' local step_ms samples; the reported score is the median over the 5 repeats of those aligned maxima. Rank-local times are never summed across ranks, and the gloo control barrier is excluded from step time (README.md:45).

Performance constraint retained from the source (workloads.json:30 step_ms_max_baseline_ratio=1.05; README.md:48 requires clean step <= 1.05x original baseline; user goal retains it): step_ms under the same max-rank-then-median aggregation must be <= 1.05x the original baseline's step_ms, where the baseline is the unmodified source implementation measured under the identical workload, precision, world_size and aggregation.

Required quality gates, all executed once by the source before any timing (gpt2_ddp_training.py:64-96) and binding on any candidate implementation: (1) finite_loss - the accumulated step loss is finite; (2) global_batch_gradient_check - full post-accumulation gradients must match a single-process (no DDP) reference that serially consumes the exact same global batch (both ranks' microbatches in rank order) within grad_atol=0.000001/grad_rtol=0.0001; (3) corrupted_output_rejected - the checker's negative control must reject a +1 corruption of reference gradients; (4) exact_gradient_replica_check - every parameter's gradient must be exactly identical on both ranks (torch.testing.assert_close with atol=0.0, rtol=0.0 against rank 0's broadcast values, :80-86); (5) parameter_update_check - parameters after the SGD step must match the reference update within parameter_atol=0.000001/parameter_rtol=0.0001. These thresholds are fixed by workloads.json:33 and must not be loosened.

Baseline implementation choices (not frozen requirements; semantics-equivalent alternatives are allowed provided the workload shape, FP32 precision, effective batch 8, 1024 tokens/step, quality gates and completion boundary are preserved): DDP options bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True, broadcast_buffers=False (:59); no_sync() on the first 3 of 4 microbatches (:40) - the requirement is the final gradient values, not the sync pattern; SGD foreach=False (:60); torch.set_num_threads(4) and interop threads 1 (common.py:35-36); the gloo control group for barriers and object gathering (:53). The SGD update rule (lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0) together with the 1/accumulation_steps loss scaling defines the enforced update semantics via the parameter_update_check.

Communication diagnostic (separately profiled; not the primary score and carrying no constraint of its own): with --profile the source runs 3 additional invocations of the same step under torch.profiler after reset and a control barrier, outside all clean timing (gpt2_ddp_training.py:121-125; common.py:87-105). Per profiled invocation it computes each rank's sum of device NCCL kernel durations (nccl_kernel_sum_ms), takes the maximum across ranks, then the median of the 3 values (diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms, :155-157). This maps to the installed torch_communication collector field communication_kernel_sum_ms (per-rank value; the evaluator applies max-across-ranks then median-of-3). Per workloads.json:34 and the collector definition, the quantity includes device waiting and is not wire time, critical-path time or exposed communication.

Recorded but unscored: peak_allocated_bytes per repeat (per-process PyTorch CUDA allocated peak, max across ranks in combined samples, gpt2_ddp_training.py:115/:119/:152; not a goal for this workload) and a one-off separate_hook_inventory pass that registers a default-allreduce comm hook to record per-rank bucket count/bytes (:128-138), explicitly outside the clean timing and the default reducer.

Devices and launch: exactly 2 GPUs are required (world_size=2 asserted at gpt2_ddp_training.py:56-57; --nproc_per_node=2; deployment inventory: 2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090). The compute process group uses NCCL (dist.init_process_group('nccl'), :52); a separate gloo group (:53) handles control barriers and record gathering. Rank/device binding, process launch and group initialization are evaluator-worker responsibilities; tool paths, GPU UUIDs and lease settings come from deployment.json.

One measured invocation: Execute one complete accumulated GPT-2 training step (source function step(), gpt2_ddp_training.py:102-105) identically on both ranks of the 2-process NCCL DDP launch. Unit of work: starting from the restored seeded initial state (gradients zeroed), run accumulate() (gpt2_ddp_training.py:36-45) = optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True), then 4 microbatch forward+backward passes (accumulation_steps=4; per rank micro_batch=1 sequence of sequence_length=128 seeded synthetic token IDs, GPU-resident, vocab 50257) through GPT2LMHeadModel in FP32 (GPT-2 124M: n_layer=12, n_embd=768, n_head=12, n_positions=1024; dropout 0; use_cache=False; labels=tokens; per-microbatch loss divided by 4), accumulating local gradients. The baseline runs the first 3 microbatches under model.no_sync() and performs the DDP gradient allreduce on the 4th; the no_sync pattern is baseline behavior, while the required semantics is that after the final microbatch both ranks hold exactly identical full gradients equal to the serially computed global batch (8 sequences x 128 tokens = 1024 tokens, effective batch 8). Then apply the SGD update (lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0) to all parameters in place, then torch.cuda.synchronize() on the rank's device. Outputs of the unit: in-place updated FP32 parameters and post-allreduce gradients exactly identical on both ranks. Completion boundary: step() returns after the synchronize on every rank. Excluded from the unit (harness/setup/reset per source gpt2_ddp_training.py:107-125): model/optimizer/input construction, initial-state restoration, pre-timer CUDA synchronize + gloo control barrier + peak-memory-stat reset, one-time reference construction and all correctness checks, the 3 separately profiled diagnostic invocations, the bucket-inventory pass, and report writing.

request.goal: Minimize maximum-rank clean step_ms for the source's complete accumulated training step, taking aligned rank maxima before the median over repeats. Retain the original step_ms <= 1.05x original-baseline constraint, all workload, precision, full quality and exact rank-replica requirements and the completion boundary. Communication kernel duration remains a separately profiled diagnostic, not wire time or the primary score.
notes: Measured unit and boundary (source-required): step_ms is the per-rank host wall time around step() (time.perf_counter_ns, gpt2_ddp_training.py:116-118); per aligned repeat index the max across the 2 ranks is taken, then the median over the 5 repeats (gpt2_ddp_training.py:149-152; common.py:66-71). README.md:45 confirms max across ranks (never summing rank times) and that the gloo control barrier is excluded from step time.

Launch provenance: user command 'torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=2 gpt2_ddp_training.py --output /tmp/original-ddp-step --profile'; README.md:37 and run_suite.py:37-40 show the equivalent 'python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nnodes=1 --nproc-per-node=2' launch with both GPUs visible, OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 and a 900 s timeout. warmup=2 and repeats=5 are the source defaults (common.py:24-25), not overridden by the command; the entry itself requires world_size == workload world_size == 2 (gpt2_ddp_training.py:56-57).

Source-required numerics: FP32 everywhere; TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn; cudnn.benchmark False; float32_matmul_precision 'highest'; GPT-2 124M (12 layers, 768 hidden, 12 heads, vocab 50257, n_positions 1024) built with dropout 0, use_cache=False, attn_implementation='eager'; torch.set_num_threads(4), interop 1 (common.py:34-42; gpt2_ddp_training.py:24-27).

Source-required workload data: deterministic synthetic weights (torch.manual_seed(20261020)) and per-rank inputs (torch.Generator seed 31000+source_rank, randint [0,50257), four (1,128) token tensors per rank, moved to the rank's GPU once outside timing); effective batch 8 = 2 ranks x micro_batch 1 x 4 accumulation steps; 1024 tokens per step (gpt2_ddp_training.py:30-33,148; README.md:44). No pretrained checkpoint or real corpus is involved (module docstring, gpt2_ddp_training.py:1-5).

Baseline implementation choices, not frozen requirements; semantics-preserving alternatives are acceptable provided every quality and exact-replica check still passes: DDP(bucket_cap_mb=25, broadcast_buffers=False, gradient_as_bucket_view=True) (gpt2_ddp_training.py:59); foreach=False in SGD (gpt2_ddp_training.py:60); the no_sync accumulation schedule itself (docstring: 'The baseline already uses no_sync accumulation') — the binding semantics are one optimizer step over the accumulated global batch whose rank-averaged gradients match the serial reference. The SGD update values (lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0) are pinned in value by the post-step parameter check against the reference optimizer (gpt2_ddp_training.py:70,88-91), not by implementation flags.
